newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bank PBI sees sale by end March.
newsitem.headline: Polish bank PBI sees sale by end March.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, will likely choose a strategic investor for its Polish Investment Bank SA (PBI) by the end of March, PBI's spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
Anna Rybaltowska told Reuters that investors had until the end of January to submit final bids for a majority stake and that several domestic and foreign investors had shown interest.
"We're counting on the choice (of the investor) to be decided at the end of March," Rybaltowska said.

Late last month the central bank would not confirm a report in the daily Rzeczpospolita that it had shortlisted three banks bidding for PBI and Prosper Bank SA -- Kredyt Bank, GE Capital and Creditanstalt Bank SA.
It said some of the information in the newspaper report was true, some false, but would not elaborate.

PBI, recently awarded a BBB- long-term rating by IBCA, made an 85.1-million- zloty pre-tax profit over the first three quarters of 1996 and expected to make a pre-tax profit of 100 million that year and a net profit of more than 60 million.
In 1995 PBI had a net profit of 26.2 million zlotys.

PBI, carved out of the NBP in 1993 with a clean credit portfolio, remains 100-percent owned by the central bank. The NBP took control of more than 90 percent of ailing Prosper Bank in 1993 as a result of a bail-out scheme and has since retained its stake to guide the bank's turnaround.
